requirements.text: Stuff the paper into the cup.
requirements.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup

outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Is there visible evidence that the paper has progressed toward being placed into the cup, such as being positioned at or partly inside an identifiable cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the image visibly shows the paper positioned at or partly inside an identifiable cup, indicating progress toward placement. Fail only when both paper and cup are identifiable and the image clearly shows no progress toward placing the paper in the cup. Unknown if either object or their relevant placement cannot be identified, or the evidence is ambiguous.
nodes.binding: Assess only the requested paper-into-cup placement in the edited image. Do not infer progress from proximity to an unidentified object, and do not use the reference label or unsupported descriptions.

nodes.question: When the paper and cup are identifiable, does the image show the paper fully inside the cup and visibly stuffed into it, rather than merely at the opening, on the rim, or nearby?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if visible evidence establishes that the paper is inside the identifiable cup and has been stuffed into it. Fail if the paper and cup are identifiable and the image clearly establishes that this completed placement is not present. Unknown if the cup, paper, or their relation cannot be assessed, or if the evidence does not resolve whether stuffing is complete.
nodes.binding: Investigate completion of the requested paper-in-cup placement from the edited image itself. A progress observation is context only; independently verify the objects and their spatial relation. Do not treat proximity or rim contact as completion.

nodes.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
nodes.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Complete only when s3 passes. Partial only when s1 passes and s3 fails, establishing progress and clear incompleteness. Absent only when s1 fails, establishing assessable no progress. If either necessary observation is unknown, or the observations do not establish one of these cases, report unknown. Do not infer visual facts beyond the saved observations.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks overlap and contradict one another in their composition. s2 is nested under s3 but asks whether the same completion is determinable, while its criteria classify clear non-completion as fail and ambiguity as unknown; it adds no distinct evidence needed by the readout. More importantly, fulfillment treats s3 fail as sufficient for partial whenever s1 passes, although s3 can fail because completion is clearly absent without establishing that the paper has progressed toward stuffing. The readout therefore can infer partial without the required progress evidence. Its parent chain also makes fulfillment activation depend on s2, despite s2 being only a redundant determinability check. Reject."}
